- Consolidated data - Important financial bodies in different sphere like ministries, darparments, etc -
Financial Body Sphere Parent Organization Establishment Year Purpose Additional Details
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Central Bank Ministry of Finance 1935 (Nationalized: 1949) Monetary policy, banking regulation, currency issuance, financial stability Manages ~₹60 lakh crore assets (2025). Regulates CRR, SLR, Repo Rate (4.4% as of Aug 2025). Established under RBI Act, 1934. Recent: Launched PIDF for digital payments, harmonized LCR for foreign banks.
Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) Ministry Department Ministry of Finance 1947 Formulates economic policies, Union Budget, public debt management Handles ~₹30 lakh crore budget (2025). Oversees SPMCIL, foreign aid (~₹50,000 crore FDI 2025). Abolished FIPB in 2017. Manages IES cadre.
Department of Expenditure Ministry Department Ministry of Finance 1947 Manages government expenditure, financial discipline Oversees ~₹50 lakh crore expenditure (2025). Implements 7th CPC, manages NIFM. Excludes GoI borrowing. Recent: Gati Shakti funding (~₹10 lakh crore).
Department of Revenue Ministry Department Ministry of Finance 1947 Administers tax policies, GST, customs Collects ~₹28 lakh crore tax revenue (2025). Oversees CBDT, CBIC. Recent: Faceless tax assessment, GST reforms.
Department of Financial Services (DFS) Ministry Department Ministry of Finance 1947 Regulates banks, insurance, financial inclusion Oversees ~₹120 lakh crore banking assets (2025). Promotes PMJDY (~50 crore accounts), MUDRA (~₹20 lakh crore loans). Recent: Bank mergers (e.g., PNB-OBC).
Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Ministry Department Ministry of Finance 1996 Manages disinvestment, CPSE investments Handles ~₹6 lakh crore disinvestment (2025). Key in LIC IPO (~₹21,000 crore). Recent: Asset monetization (~₹2 lakh crore).
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Regulatory Body Ministry of Finance 1988 (Statutory: 1992) Regulates securities markets, investor protection Oversees ~₹450 lakh crore market cap (2025). Merged with FMC in 2015. Recent: ESG disclosures, REIT regulations.
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) Regulatory Body Ministry of Finance 1999 Regulates insurance industry, policyholder protection Manages ~₹60 lakh crore insurance market (2025). Recent: Bima Sakhi Yojana, video KYC norms. Regulates FDI (74% cap).
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) Regulatory Body Ministry of Finance 2003 Regulates pension funds, oversees NPS Manages ~₹12 lakh crore NPS assets (2025). Covers ~17 million subscribers. Recent: NPS expansion to informal sector.
National Housing Bank (NHB) Regulatory Body Ministry of Finance (post-2019) 1988 Regulates housing finance, supports HFIs Financed ~₹20,000 crore housing loans (2025). Recent: Special Housing Fund for EWS. Transferred from RBI to MoF in 2019.
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) Development Finance Institution Ministry of Finance 1990 Finances MSMEs, promotes microfinance Disbursed ~₹25,000 crore to MSMEs (2025). Supports PM MUDRA, CGTMSE. Recent: MSME digital lending platform.
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) Development Finance Institution Ministry of Finance 1982 Refinances rural credit, promotes agriculture Refinanced ~₹60,000 crore rural credit (2025). Supports RRBs, PACS, PM-KISAN. Recent: Climate-resilient agriculture funding.
Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) Development Finance Institution Ministry of Finance 1948 Provides long-term industrial finance Financed ~₹15,000 crore industries (2025). Oldest DFI. Recent: Focus on green energy projects.
Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) Development Finance Institution (now Bank) Ministry of Finance (pre-1990s) 1955 Industrial finance (pre-2002), now commercial banking Financed ~₹60,000 crore pre-privatization (1995). Privatized in 2002, now manages ~₹20 lakh crore assets (2025).
Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) Development Finance Institution (now Bank) Ministry of Finance (pre-2000s) 1964 Industrial finance, now commercial banking Financed ~₹1.5 lakh crore industries pre-privatization (2002). Privatized in 2023 (LIC-led). Manages ~₹10 lakh crore assets (2025).
Finance Commission Constitutional Body Ministry of Finance 1951 Recommends tax revenue distribution, grants-in-aid 15th FC (2021–26) allocated ~41% taxes to States (~₹12 lakh crore). Recent: Disaster management grants.
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) Regulatory Body Ministry of Corporate Affairs 2016 Implements IBC, regulates insolvency processes Resolved ~6,000 cases by 2025 (~₹4 lakh crore). Recent: Pre-packaged insolvency for MSMEs.
Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) Ministry Government of India 2006 Regulates corporate governance, Companies Act Oversees ~27 lakh companies (2025). Enforces Competition Act, 2002. Recent: Decriminalized minor offenses.
Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) Industry Association SEBI 1995 Promotes mutual fund industry, investor education Manages ~₹50 lakh crore AUM (2025). Recent: “Mutual Funds Sahi Hai” campaign.
Unit Trust of India (UTI) Financial Institution Ministry of Finance (pre-2003) 1964 Mutual fund and investment services Managed ~₹15,000 crore assets (1995). Split into UTI MF, SUUTI in 2003. UTI MF manages ~₹20 lakh crore (2025).
Banking Ombudsman Grievance Redressal Body Reserve Bank of India 1995 Resolves banking complaints, free service Handled ~15,000 cases in 2025. Recent: Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021. Non-binding orders.
Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank) Development Finance Institution Ministry of Finance 1982 Finances export-import trade Disbursed ~₹1.2 lakh crore for trade (2025). Recent: Green trade financing. Supports EXIM Policy.
National Stock Exchange (NSE) Stock Exchange SEBI 1992 Facilitates equity, derivatives trading Handles ~₹350 lakh crore market cap (2025). Key index: Nifty 50. Recent: ESG index launch.
Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) Stock Exchange SEBI 1875 Facilitates equity, debt trading Manages ~₹120 lakh crore market cap (2025). Key index: Sensex. Recent: Green bond platform.
Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) Appellate Body Ministry of Finance 1995 Hears appeals against SEBI orders Resolves ~1,200 cases annually (2025). Recent: Digital hearing platform.
Forward Markets Commission (FMC) Regulatory Body (Defunct) Ministry of Finance (pre-2015) 1953 (Merged with SEBI: 2015) Regulated commodity futures (pre-2015) Oversaw ~₹60 lakh crore futures market pre-2015. Merged with SEBI (Q24 2009).
Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) Constitutional Body Ministry of Finance 1858 Audits government accounts, ensures transparency Audits ~₹55 lakh crore public funds (2025). Recent: Performance audit of PM-KISAN. UPSC: GS2 (Q5 2017).
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) Public Sector Insurance Ministry of Finance 1956 Provides life insurance, investment products Manages ~₹45 lakh crore assets (2025). Recent: Bima Sakhi Yojana for women. Largest insurer.
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) Banking Institution Ministry of Finance, NABARD 1975 Provides rural credit, financial inclusion Disbursed ~₹25,000 crore (2025). Serves ~160 million households. Recent: Digital banking push.
State Bank of India (SBI) Public Sector Bank Ministry of Finance 1955 Commercial banking, financial services Manages ~₹55 lakh crore deposits (2025). Recent: Green financing initiatives. Largest PSB.
Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) Trade Regulatory Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1991 Regulates and promotes foreign trade, issues IEC Issues ~12 lakh IECs annually (2025). Recent: RoDTEP scheme extension.
Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) Export Credit Insurance Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1957 Provides export credit insurance, risk cover Covers ~₹12,000 crore exports annually (2025). Recent: Enhanced MSME export cover.
Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1965 Promotes exports, provides market intelligence Supports ~22,000 exporters (2025). Recent: Digital trade platform launch.
India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1977 Organizes trade fairs, promotes exports Hosts ~60 trade fairs annually (2025). Recent: Bharat Tex 2025 event.
Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1972 Promotes marine product exports Supports ~₹60,000 crore marine exports (2025). Recent: Sustainable aquaculture push.
Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1985 Promotes agricultural, processed food exports Facilitates ~₹1.2 lakh crore exports (2025). Recent: Organic export certification.
Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1966 Promotes gem, jewellery exports Supports ~₹2.5 lakh crore exports (2025). Recent: Lab-grown diamond focus.
Spices Board India Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1987 Promotes spice exports, quality certification Facilitates ~₹35,000 crore spice exports (2025). Recent: GI tag promotion.
Tea Board of India Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Commerce and Industry 1953 Promotes tea cultivation, exports Supports ~₹6,000 crore tea exports (2025). Recent: Tea e-auction platform.
Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) Trade Promotion Body Ministry of Textiles 1970 Promotes cotton exports, market support Handles ~₹12,000 crore cotton trade (2025). Recent: MSP procurement for farmers.
Coir Board Trade Promotion Body Ministry of MSME 1953 Promotes coir exports, product development Supports ~₹3,500 crore coir exports (2025). Recent: Coir geotextile promotion.
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) Rural Industry Promotion Ministry of MSME 1957 Promotes khadi, village industry exports Supports ~₹6,000 crore rural exports (2025). Recent: PMEGP expansion.
National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) MSME Support Body Ministry of MSME 1955 Supports MSME exports, financial aid Provides ~₹12,000 crore credit to MSMEs (2025). Recent: Single-window clearance portal.
NITI Aayog (Economics and Finance Cell) Policy Think Tank Government of India 2015 Drives economic policy reforms, financial sector analysis Appraises ~₹600 crore projects (2025). Supports G20, asset monetization (~₹2 lakh crore). Recent: Vision 2035.
Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) Tax Regulatory Body Ministry of Finance 1963 Manages customs duties, GST for trade Collects ~₹8 lakh crore customs, GST (2025). Recent: GST e-invoicing, CRCL labs.
Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council) Constitutional Body Ministry of Finance 2016 Formulates GST policies, tax rates Oversees ~₹20 lakh crore GST collections (2025). Recent: GST rate rationalization.
National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) Development Finance Institution Ministry of Finance 2021 Finances infrastructure projects Disbursed ~₹50,000 crore for infra (2025). Recent: Supports NIP projects.
India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) Development Finance Institution Ministry of Finance 2006 Provides long-term infra finance Financed ~₹1 lakh crore infra projects (2025). Recent: Green bond issuance.
Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Tax Regulatory Body Ministry of Finance 1963 Administers direct taxes, income tax policies Collects ~₹15 lakh crore income tax (2025). Recent: Faceless assessment, Vivad Se Vishwas.
National Institute of Financial Management (NIFM) Training Institute Ministry of Finance 1993 Trains financial management professionals Trains ~5,000 officers annually (2025). Recent: Digital finance courses.
Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) Appellate Body Ministry of Finance 2017 Hears appeals against GST orders Resolves ~2,000 GST cases annually (2025). Recent: Digital adjudication platform.
- Important acts and rules -
Act/Rule Category Year Purpose Key Provisions/Additional Details
Reserve Bank of India Act Banking 1934 Establishes RBI, regulates monetary policy, currency issuance Empowers RBI to formulate monetary policy, regulate banks, issue currency (~₹35 lakh crore in circulation, 2025). Establishes MPC for repo rate (4.4%, Aug 2025). Governor appointed by GoI for 3-year term. Recent: Digital currency pilot (e-Rupee, ~₹1,000 crore transactions, 2025).
Banking Regulation Act Banking 1949 Regulates banking operations, empowers RBI Defines RBI’s powers for bank licensing, minimum capital (₹500 crore for new banks), and supervision. Establishes DICGC for deposit insurance (~₹2 lakh per depositor, 2025). Recent: Co-operative bank amendments (2020) for RBI oversight. Covers ~₹150 lakh crore banking assets.
Negotiable Instruments Act Banking 1881 Governs cheques, promissory notes, bills of exchange Regulates transferability, liabilities (Section 138: cheque bounce penalties, up to 2 years imprisonment). Amended in 2018 for faster dispute resolution. Handles ~₹10 lakh crore cheque transactions annually (2025). Supports digital instruments like e-cheques.
Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) Financial Security 2002 Prevents money laundering, terrorism financing Establishes FIU-India, mandates KYC, STR reporting by banks (~50 lakh reports, 2025). Penalties: 7-year imprisonment, ~₹5,000 crore fines (2025). Recent: Crypto transactions under PMLA (2023). Administered by ED.
SARFAESI Act Banking 2002 Enables banks to recover NPAs without court intervention Allows asset seizure, sale for secured loans (>₹1 crore). Recovered ~₹3 lakh crore NPAs by 2025. Recent: Extended to NBFCs (2020). Excludes unsecured loans, agricultural land. Managed by DRTs.
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) Banking 2016 Streamlines insolvency resolution, bankruptcy processes Establishes IBBI, NCLT for 180-day resolution (~6,000 cases resolved, ₹4 lakh crore recovered, 2025). Recent: Pre-packaged insolvency for MSMEs (2021). Reduced NPAs by ~20%. Covers corporate, individual bankruptcy.
Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) Foreign Exchange 1999 Regulates foreign exchange, trade, payments Replaced FERA (1973). Empowers RBI for FDI (74% in insurance), ODI (~$700 billion forex reserves, 2025). Recent: Liberalized ECB norms (2024). Administered by DGFT, RBI. Penalties up to 3x violation amount.
Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBM) Fiscal Policy 2003 Ensures fiscal discipline, reduces fiscal deficit Targets 3% fiscal deficit, 60% debt-to-GDP ratio (~₹180 lakh crore public debt, 2025). Recent: Escape clause for crises (4.5% deficit, 2023–24). Administered by MoF, reviewed by NK Singh Committee (2017).
Goods and Services Tax Act Taxation 2017 Unifies indirect taxes, streamlines tax system Subsumed VAT, excise, service tax. Collects ~₹8 lakh crore annually (2025). Administered by GST Council, CBIC. Rates: 5–28%. Recent: E-invoicing mandatory for businesses >₹10 crore (2024). Covers ~1.4 crore taxpayers.
Income Tax Act Taxation 1961 Governs direct taxation, income tax collection Administered by CBDT, collects ~₹12 lakh crore (2025). Defines slabs (new regime: 0–30%), exemptions (Section 80C: ₹1.5 lakh). Recent: Faceless assessment (2020), Vivad Se Vishwas (2024). Covers ~7 crore ITRs.
Companies Act Corporate Governance 2013 Regulates company formation, operations, governance Oversees ~27 lakh companies (2025). Mandates CSR (2% profit), board diversity (1 woman director). Recent: Decriminalized minor offenses (2020). Administered by MCA, ROC. Replaced 1956 Act.
Competition Act Market Regulation 2002 Promotes competition, prevents monopolies Establishes CCI, regulates mergers, anti-competitive practices (~₹6,000 crore fines, 2025). Recent: Digital market regulations (2024). Replaced MRTP Act (1969). Covers cartels, abuse of dominance.
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Financial Security 2010 Regulates foreign contributions to NGOs, organizations Monitors ~₹25,000 crore foreign funds (2025). Mandates FCRA registration, SBI account for NGOs. Recent: 2020 amendment tightened compliance. Administered by MHA. Penalties: 5-year ban.
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act Market Regulation 1992 Regulates securities market, protects investors Establishes SEBI, oversees ~₹450 lakh crore market cap (2025). Recent: ESG disclosures, REIT regulations (2024). Merged with FMC (2015). Penalties up to ₹25 crore for violations.
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act Insurance 1999 Regulates insurance sector, protects policyholders Establishes IRDAI, manages ~₹60 lakh crore insurance market (2025). FDI limit raised to 74% (2021). Recent: Bima Sakhi Yojana for women agents (2024). Ensures solvency margins (150%).
National Housing Bank Act Housing Finance 1987 Regulates housing finance institutions Establishes NHB, financed ~₹20,000 crore housing loans (2025). Shifted to MoF from RBI (2019). Recent: EWS housing fund (~₹5,000 crore, 2025). Supports PMAY implementation.
SIDBI Act MSME Finance 1989 Establishes SIDBI for MSME financing Disbursed ~₹25,000 crore to MSMEs (2025). Supports MUDRA, CGTMSE. Recent: Digital lending platform for MSMEs (2024). Promotes microfinance, startup funding.
Export-Import Bank of India Act Trade Finance 1981 Finances export-import trade Establishes EXIM Bank, disbursed ~₹1.2 lakh crore for trade (2025). Recent: Green trade financing (~₹10,000 crore, 2025). Supports RoDTEP, EXIM Policy. Administered by MoF.
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act Rural Finance 1981 Promotes rural credit, agriculture financing Establishes NABARD, refinanced ~₹60,000 crore (2025). Supports RRBs, PACS, PM-KISAN. Recent: Climate-resilient agriculture funding (~₹5,000 crore, 2025). Covers ~15 crore farmers.
Industrial Finance Corporation of India Act Industrial Finance 1948 Provides long-term industrial finance Establishes IFCI, financed ~₹15,000 crore industries (2025). Oldest DFI. Recent: Green energy financing (~₹2,000 crore, 2025). Supports industrial corridors, MSMEs.
Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act Banking 1961 Provides deposit insurance, credit guarantees Insures ~₹2 lakh per depositor (2025). Covers ~₹150 lakh crore deposits. Recent: Extended to co-operative banks (2020). Protects small depositors during bank failures.
State Financial Corporations Act State Finance 1951 Establishes SFCs for state-level industrial finance Disbursed ~₹6,000 crore to MSMEs (2025). Operates in 18 states under RBI guidelines. Recent: Focus on state-level startup funding. Supports regional industrial growth.
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act Banking 1970, 1980 Nationalizes major commercial banks Nationalized 14 banks (1969), 6 banks (1980). Manages ~₹60 lakh crore deposits (2025). Recent: Bank mergers (e.g., PNB-OBC, 2020). Strengthened PSB framework.
Regional Rural Banks Act Rural Banking 1976 Establishes RRBs for rural credit Disbursed ~₹25,000 crore (2025). Serves ~160 million households via 43 RRBs. Recent: Digital banking integration (2024). Administered by NABARD, MoF.
Chit Fund Act Non-Banking Finance 1982 Regulates chit funds, protects investors Oversees ~₹12,000 crore chit fund market (2025). Mandates registration, 20% deposit with RBI. Recent: Digital chit fund regulations (2023). Administered by state governments.
Fugitive Economic Offenders Act Financial Security 2018 Addresses economic offenders fleeing India Allows asset confiscation for frauds >₹100 crore (~15 cases, ₹5,000 crore assets seized, 2025). Recent: Fast-track courts for FEOs (2023). Administered by ED, MoF.
General Financial Rules (GFR) Public Finance 2017 Governs public procurement, financial management Manages ~₹50 lakh crore expenditure (2025). Recent: 2020 amendment for border country restrictions, GeM portal mandatory for procurement (>₹5 lakh crore, 2025). Administered by MoF.
Banking Ombudsman Scheme Banking 2006 Resolves banking complaints, consumer protection Handled ~15,000 cases (2025). Free service, non-binding orders up to ₹20 lakh compensation. Recent: Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (2021). Administered by RBI.
Securities Law (Amendment) Act Market Regulation 2014 Strengthens SEBI’s powers against fraud Targets Ponzi schemes, enhances SEBI penalties (~₹7,000 crore fines, 2025). Recent: Crypto regulation framework (2024). Protects ~₹450 lakh crore market cap.
Factoring Regulation Act Financial Services 2011 Regulates factoring business, MSME financing Facilitates ~₹6,000 crore factoring market (2025). Recent: TReDS platform integration (2024, ~₹50,000 crore invoices). Administered by RBI, supports MSME liquidity.
Government Securities Act Public Debt 2006 Manages government securities market Oversees ~₹100 lakh crore G-Sec market (2025). Recent: Green bonds issuance (~₹10,000 crore, 2025). Administered by RBI, supports debt financing.
Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act Credit Regulation 2005 Regulates credit bureaus, credit scoring Oversees CIBIL, Experian (~₹120 lakh crore credit data, 2025). Recent: Data privacy norms (2023). Administered by RBI, improves credit access for ~50 crore individuals.
Public Debt Act Public Finance 1944 Governs government borrowing, debt management Manages ~₹180 lakh crore public debt (2025). Recent: Sovereign green bonds (~₹5,000 crore, 2025). Administered by RBI, MoF. Supports fiscal policy.
Central Excise Act Taxation 1944 Regulates excise duties on goods Largely subsumed by GST (2017). Collected ~₹2.5 lakh crore pre-GST (2016). Administered by CBIC. Applies to petroleum, tobacco post-GST. Revenue ~₹50,000 crore (2025).
Customs Act Trade Taxation 1962 Governs customs duties, import-export taxation Collects ~₹1.8 lakh crore customs duties (2025). Administered by CBIC. Recent: AEO programme for trade facilitation (2024). Supports RoDTEP, EXIM Policy.
Bankers’ Books Evidence Act Banking 1891 Regulates banking records as legal evidence Used in ~1 lakh financial disputes annually (2025). Amended in 2000 for digital records. Supports fraud investigations, loan recovery cases. Administered by RBI, courts.
Co-operative Societies Act Cooperative Finance 1912 Regulates cooperative societies, banks Oversees ~₹6 lakh crore cooperative sector (2025). Recent: 2023 amendment for co-operative banks under RBI. Supports ~1 crore PACS, rural finance.
Life Insurance Corporation Act Insurance 1956 Establishes LIC, regulates life insurance Manages ~₹45 lakh crore assets (2025). Recent: Bima Sakhi Yojana for women agents (2024). Nationalized 245 insurers. Largest insurer, ~70% market share.
State Bank of India Act Banking 1955 Establishes SBI, regulates its operations Manages ~₹55 lakh crore deposits (2025). Recent: Green financing initiatives (~₹5,000 crore, 2025). Largest PSB, ~25% banking market share. Administered by MoF.
Central Sales Tax Act Taxation 1956 Regulates inter-state sales taxation Largely subsumed by GST (2017). Collected ~₹60,000 crore pre-GST (2016). Administered by CBIC. Applies to non-GST goods like petroleum (~₹10,000 crore, 2025).
Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act Taxation 2021 Amends tax laws, removes retrospective taxation Resolved ~₹10,000 crore tax disputes (2025). Recent: Settled Vodafone, Cairn cases (2022). Boosts FDI confidence, administered by CBDT.
Payment and Settlement Systems Act Banking 2007 Regulates payment systems, digital transactions Empowers RBI to regulate UPI, NEFT (~₹2,000 lakh crore transactions, 2025). Establishes NPCI. Recent: UPI international expansion (2024). Ensures payment security.
Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) Housing Finance 2016 Regulates real estate, protects homebuyers Establishes state-level RERAs, mandates project registration (~50,000 projects, 2025). Recent: Online complaint portals (2023). Administered by MoHUA, protects ~₹5 lakh crore investments.
Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act Financial Security 1988 (Amended 2016) Prohibits benami property transactions Seized ~₹20,000 crore benami assets (2025). Recent: 2016 amendment increased penalties (7-year imprisonment). Administered by CBDT, ED. Targets tax evasion, black money.
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act Pension 2013 Regulates pension funds, oversees NPS Establishes PFRDA, manages ~₹12 lakh crore NPS assets (2025). Recent: NPS for informal sector (2024). Covers ~17 million subscribers, promotes retirement security.
Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) Act Financial Security 2015 Addresses undisclosed foreign assets, tax evasion Imposes 30–90% tax, 7-year imprisonment. Recovered ~₹5,000 crore (2025). Recent: Global tax treaty integration (2023). Administered by CBDT, ED.
National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development Act Infrastructure Finance 2021 Establishes NaBFID for infrastructure financing Disbursed ~₹50,000 crore for NIP projects (2025). Recent: Green infra bonds (~₹5,000 crore, 2025). Administered by MoF, supports Gati Shakti.
Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act Market Regulation 1956 Regulates stock exchanges, securities contracts Empowers SEBI to regulate BSE, NSE (~₹450 lakh crore market cap, 2025). Recent: T+1 settlement cycle (2023). Ensures market transparency, investor protection.
Finance Act Fiscal Policy Annual (e.g., 2025) Implements Union Budget, amends tax laws Amends Income Tax, GST, Customs Acts annually (~₹30 lakh crore budget, 2025). Recent: Simplified tax regime (2025). Administered by MoF, CBDT, CBIC.
Payment of Bonus Act Labour Finance 1965 Mandates bonus payments to employees Ensures 8.33–20% bonus for employees earning <₹21,000/month. Covers ~5 crore workers (2025). Recent: Linked to productivity (2023). Administered by MoLE.
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act Pension 1952 Provides social security via PF, pension, insurance Manages ~₹20 lakh crore PF corpus (2025). Covers ~7 crore employees. Recent: E-nomination mandatory (2024). Administered by EPFO, MoLE.
- Important government policies relatred to different spahers -
Policy Sphere Year Objective Key Features and Details Eligibility and Impact
National Agricultural Policy Agriculture 2000 Promote sustainable agriculture, enhance productivity, and ensure food security Focuses on increasing agricultural growth rate to 4%, promoting crop diversification, improving irrigation, and supporting farmer credit systems. Emphasizes private sector participation, technology adoption, and sustainable practices like organic farming. Includes provisions for women farmers through 30% fund allocation. Targets ~15 crore farmers. Impacts ~₹5 lakh crore farm output (2023). Benefits women farmers via schemes like MKSP. UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
National Policy for Farmers Agriculture 2007 Improve farmer livelihoods, increase farm income, and ensure economic security Based on M.S. Swaminathan’s recommendations, it emphasizes minimum support prices (MSP), crop insurance, and credit access. Promotes women’s role in agriculture through SHGs and FPOs. Includes measures for drought/flood resilience and biosecurity. Eligible: All farmers, including small/marginal. Impacts ~150 million farmers, ~₹2 lakh crore MSP procurement (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy, Agriculture).
National Food Security Policy Food Security 2013 Ensure affordable food access for the poor, reduce hunger Linked to NFSA, provides subsidized food grains through PDS to 67% of population. Prioritizes women-headed households for ration cards. Includes nutritional support for pregnant women and children via ICDS. Eligible: ~80 crore BPL families. Distributes ~₹2 lakh crore food subsidies annually (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
National Policy for Women Gender Equality 2016 Empower women, ensure gender equity, and promote equal opportunities Envisions equal participation in socio-economic and political spheres. Focuses on education, health, economic empowerment, and safety. Supports schemes like BBBP, PMMVY, and Mahila E-Haat. Promotes legal reforms and gender budgeting. Eligible: All women, especially marginalized. Impacts ~₹50,000 crore women-centric schemes (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
National Health Policy Health 2017 Achieve universal health coverage, improve healthcare access Targets 2.5% GDP spending on health by 2025. Strengthens PHCs, promotes preventive care, and integrates AYUSH. Supports schemes like Ayushman Bharat and JSY. Emphasizes maternal and child health. Eligible: All citizens, focus on BPL. Covers ~50 crore via Ayushman Bharat (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
National Education Policy (NEP) Education 2020 Transform education system, promote holistic learning Introduces 5+3+3+4 structure, emphasizes vocational education, and targets 6% GDP spending. Promotes girls’ education through schemes like BBBP and KGBV. Focuses on digital learning and teacher training. Eligible: All students. Impacts ~25 crore students, ~₹1 lakh crore education budget (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Education).
National Housing Policy Housing 1998 (Revised 2007) Ensure affordable housing for all citizens Promotes public-private partnerships, slum rehabilitation, and rural housing. Supports PMAY for urban/rural housing. Encourages women’s property ownership through joint titles. Eligible: EWS/LIG families. Built ~2 crore houses under PMAY (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Urban Development).
National Urban Housing and Habitat Policy Housing 2007 Address urban housing shortages, promote sustainable habitats Focuses on affordable urban housing, slum redevelopment, and smart cities. Supports PMAY-U, provides subsidies for EWS/LIG. Encourages women’s property rights. Eligible: Urban poor. Impacts ~₹1 lakh crore urban housing projects (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Urbanization).
National Policy on Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Skill Development 2015 Enhance employability, promote entrepreneurship Aligns with PMKVY, promotes industry-relevant skills, and supports women/SHG entrepreneurship. Establishes NSDA and Sector Skill Councils. Targets 40 crore skilled youth by 2022. Eligible: Youth, women, unemployed. Trained ~1.2 crore under PMKVY (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
National Policy on Electronics Industry 2019 Promote electronics manufacturing, boost digital economy Targets $400 billion industry by 2025. Supports PLI schemes, promotes women in tech through training programs. Focuses on IoT, AI, and semiconductor production. Eligible: MSMEs, startups. Supports ~₹50,000 crore PLI investments (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Industry).
National Policy on MSMEs MSME 2006 Promote MSME growth, competitiveness, and job creation Provides credit, technology, and market access. Supports women entrepreneurs via Udyogini, PMEGP. Promotes clusters and FPOs for scale. Eligible: ~6 crore MSMEs. Contributes ~₹20 lakh crore to GDP (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
National Policy on Disaster Management Disaster Management 2009 Strengthen disaster preparedness, mitigation, and response Establishes NDMA, promotes community-based disaster management. Includes women in relief planning and rehabilitation. Focuses on climate-resilient infrastructure. Eligible: All citizens. Manages ~₹1 lakh crore relief funds (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Disaster Management).
National Policy on Biofuels Energy 2018 Promote biofuel production, ensure energy security Targets 20% ethanol blending by 2025. Supports farmers through biomass supply chains. Promotes women SHGs in biofuel production. Eligible: Farmers, SHGs. Supports ~₹10,000 crore projects (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Energy).
National Water Policy Water Resources 2012 Ensure sustainable water management and equitable access Promotes water conservation, efficient irrigation (PMKSY), and river basin management. Prioritizes women in community water management programs. Eligible: All citizens. Supports ~₹5 lakh crore water projects (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Environment).
National Policy for Rare Diseases Health 2021 Address treatment and affordability for rare diseases Provides financial aid up to ₹50 lakh per patient. Establishes Centers of Excellence for diagnosis and treatment. Supports women and children disproportionately affected. Eligible: Rare disease patients. Impacts ~1 crore patients (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
National Policy on Child Labour Social Welfare 1987 Eliminate child labour, protect child rights Prohibits hazardous work for children under 14. Supports education and rehabilitation. Aligns with RTE and ICDS for girl child welfare. Eligible: Children under 14. Impacts ~1 crore children (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
National Policy for Senior Citizens Social Welfare 1999 (Revised 2011) Ensure welfare, financial security for senior citizens Provides pensions, healthcare, and social security via NSAP. Includes women-specific provisions for widows and destitute elderly. Eligible: Elderly above 60. Supports ~10 crore elderly (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
National Policy on Marine Fisheries Fisheries 2017 Promote sustainable fisheries, boost marine exports Supports modern fishing techniques, women SHGs in fish processing, and export promotion. Aligns with PMMSY for infrastructure development. Eligible: Fisherfolk. Supports ~₹50,000 crore exports (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
National Policy on Renewable Energy Energy 2006 (Revised 2015) Promote renewable energy, reduce carbon emissions Targets 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030. Supports solar, wind projects, and women-led clean energy initiatives via PM-KUSUM. Eligible: All citizens, farmers. Supports ~₹2 lakh crore investments (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Environment).
National Policy on Cooperatives Cooperatives 2002 Promote cooperative movement, support rural economy Encourages women-led cooperatives, supports agricultural and dairy cooperatives. Provides financial and technical support to ~8 lakh cooperatives. Eligible: Cooperative members. Impacts ~₹5 lakh crore cooperative sector (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
National Youth Policy Youth Development 2014 Empower youth, promote skill development, and civic engagement Focuses on education, employment, and health for youth aged 15–29. Includes women-specific programs like SAG and NYLP for leadership. Eligible: Youth aged 15–29. Impacts ~40 crore youth (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
- Important government schemes and programmes -
Scheme/Programme Sphere Year Objective Key Features and Details Eligibility and Impact
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) Agriculture 2019 Provide direct income support to farmers Offers ₹6,000/year in three ₹2,000 installments via DBT to small/marginal farmers. Supports agricultural inputs and financial stability. Includes women farmers with land ownership. Eligible: Farmers with up to 2 hectares. Benefits ~12 crore farmers, disbursed ~₹2.5 lakh crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) Fisheries 2020 Promote sustainable fisheries, boost fish production Invests ₹20,050 crore (2020–25) for infrastructure like hatcheries, ponds, and testing labs. Supports women SHGs in fish processing and marketing. Targets 70 lakh tonnes fish production by 2025. Eligible: Fisherfolk, SHGs. Impacts ~₹50,000 crore exports (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) Agriculture 2016 Provide crop insurance against natural calamities Offers low-premium insurance for crops, covering risks like drought, floods. Premium: 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi. Includes women farmers under 30% fund allocation. Eligible: All farmers. Covers ~5.5 crore farmers, disbursed ~₹1 lakh crore claims (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) Agriculture 2015 Enhance irrigation, improve water use efficiency Promotes drip/sprinkler irrigation with subsidies (up to 90%). Includes “Per Drop More Crop” and watershed development. Supports women farmers via SHGs. Eligible: All farmers. Irrigates ~50 lakh hectares, ~₹50,000 crore invested (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
PM-KUSUM Scheme Agriculture/Energy 2019 Promote solar energy in agriculture Provides up to 90% subsidy for solar pumps and solarization of 10,000 MW grid-connected plants. Supports women farmers through cooperative models. Eligible: Farmers, cooperatives. Installed ~2 lakh solar pumps (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Environment).
Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP) Agriculture/Women 2011 Empower women farmers through skill and financial support Under NRLM, provides training in sustainable agriculture, credit access, and FPO formation. Focuses on organic farming and market linkages for women. Eligible: Women farmers, SHGs. Empowers ~2 crore women farmers (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Rashtriya Mahila Kisan Yojana Agriculture/Women 2010 Encourage women farmers’ leadership in agriculture Provides technical training, leadership development, and market access. Supports women in adopting modern farming techniques and forming cooperatives. Eligible: Women farmers. Impacts ~1 crore women farmers (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana Agriculture 2025 Enhance agricultural productivity, rural prosperity Covers 100 low-productivity districts with focus on crop diversification, post-harvest storage, and irrigation. Supports women farmers through 30% fund allocation. Eligible: Farmers in targeted districts. Targets ~1.7 crore farmers, ~₹50,000 crore investment by 2031. UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses Agriculture 2025 Achieve self-sufficiency in pulses production 6-year program focusing on tur, urad, masoor. Develops climate-resilient seeds, ensures procurement at MSP, and supports women farmers via SHGs. Eligible: Pulse farmers. Targets ~₹10,000 crore production (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Comprehensive Programme for Vegetables & Fruits Agriculture 2025 Enhance vegetable/fruit production and farmer income Promotes processing, marketing, and FPO formation. Supports women in horticulture through training and credit access. Eligible: Horticulture farmers. Supports ~₹20,000 crore market (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
National Mission on High Yielding Seeds Agriculture 2025 Improve crop productivity and pest resilience Releases 100+ seed varieties since 2024. Strengthens seed research and commercial availability. Includes women farmers in seed distribution programs. Eligible: All farmers. Impacts ~₹5,000 crore seed market (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Mission for Cotton Productivity Agriculture 2025 Boost extra-long staple cotton productivity 5-year program promoting sustainable practices, technology, and textile supply chain. Supports women in cotton processing and cooperatives. Eligible: Cotton farmers. Strengthens ~₹10,000 crore textile exports (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme Agriculture 1998 Provide affordable credit for farming needs Offers loans up to ₹5 lakh (enhanced in 2025) for inputs like seeds, fertilizers. Includes women farmers and supports fisheries/animal husbandry. Eligible: Farmers, fishers. Disbursed ~₹20 lakh crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Soil Health Card Scheme Agriculture 2015 Improve soil fertility, enhance crop yield Provides soil testing and recommendations for fertilizers/crops. Supports women farmers through awareness programs and SHGs. Eligible: All farmers. Issued ~15 crore cards (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Agriculture 2020 Develop post-harvest infrastructure ₹1 lakh crore fund for warehouses, cold storages, and processing units. Offers 3% interest subvention. Supports women-led FPOs. Eligible: Farmers, FPOs. Financed ~₹50,000 crore projects (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Krishi Udan Scheme Agriculture/Aviation 2020 Enhance transport of agricultural produce Facilitates air transport of perishable goods like fruits, vegetables, and flowers. Subsidizes 50% freight charges. Supports women farmers via FPOs. Eligible: Farmers, exporters. Transports ~50,000 tonnes annually (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) Aviation 2016 Promote regional air connectivity, affordable air travel Subsidizes airfares (₹2,500/hour cap), connects 120 new routes (2025). Supports women employees in aviation and farmers via Krishi Udan integration. Eligible: All citizens. Served ~4 crore passengers (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Infrastructure).
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) Poverty Alleviation 2006 Guarantee 100 days of wage employment to rural households Provides unskilled manual work, prioritizes women (33% reservation). Focuses on asset creation like water conservation, roads. Wages linked to CPI-AL. Eligible: Rural households. Employs ~10 crore households, ~₹1 lakh crore wages (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) Housing 2015 Provide affordable housing for all by 2022 Offers subsidies up to ₹2.5 lakh for EWS/LIG. PMAY-G (rural) and PMAY-U (urban) promote women’s property ownership via joint titles. Eligible: EWS/LIG families. Built ~2 crore houses (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Urban Development).
SWAMIH Fund 2 Housing 2025 Complete stalled housing projects ₹15,000 crore fund to complete 1 lakh dwelling units. Prioritizes EWS/LIG, supports women’s property ownership. Eligible: Homebuyers, developers. Impacts ~₹15,000 crore projects (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Urban Development).
Ayushman Bharat Yojana Health 2018 Provide health insurance, strengthen healthcare Offers ₹5 lakh/family/year for hospitalization (PM-JAY) and strengthens PHCs/HWCs. Prioritizes women and children for maternal care. Eligible: ~50 crore BPL families. Treated ~5 crore patients (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) Health 2005 Improve rural healthcare access and quality Strengthens PHCs, deploys ASHA workers, and supports JSY/PMMVY. Focuses on maternal/child health and disease control. Eligible: Rural population. Supports ~₹50,000 crore healthcare (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
National Urban Health Mission (NUHM) Health 2013 Enhance urban healthcare for the poor Strengthens urban PHCs, focuses on slum dwellers, and supports women’s health programs like JSY. Provides mobile medical units. Eligible: Urban poor. Supports ~10 crore beneficiaries, ~₹10,000 crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) Health/Women 2005 Promote institutional deliveries, reduce maternal mortality Provides cash incentives (₹1,400 rural, ₹1,000 urban) for hospital deliveries. Supports BPL women and ASHA workers. Eligible: Pregnant women (BPL). Reduced MMR to 97/100,000 (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) Health/Women 2017 Support pregnant/lactating mothers, improve health Provides ₹5,000 in three installments for first live birth. Promotes nutrition and institutional delivery. Linked to JSY. Eligible: Pregnant women (first child). Benefits ~2 crore women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Poshan Abhiyaan Health/Nutrition 2018 Address malnutrition among women and children Targets anemia reduction, promotes community nutrition programs, and uses technology (POSHAN Tracker). Supports women via ICDS. Eligible: Women, children under 6. Impacts ~10 crore beneficiaries (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 Health/Nutrition 2021 Enhance nutritional support for women and children Upgrades Anganwadis, provides nutrition to 8 crore children, 1 crore pregnant/lactating women, and 20 lakh adolescent girls. Eligible: Children, women. Invests ~₹20,000 crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) Financial Inclusion 2014 Promote banking access, financial inclusion Offers zero-balance accounts, overdraft up to ₹10,000, and RuPay cards. Prioritizes women (50% accounts). Linked to DBT for schemes. Eligible: All citizens. Opened ~50 crore accounts, ~₹2 lakh crore deposits (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) MSME 2015 Provide loans to micro-enterprises, promote entrepreneurship Offers loans up to ₹10 lakh (Shishu, Kishor, Tarun categories). 70% beneficiaries are women. Supports SHGs and startups. Eligible: Micro-entrepreneurs. Disbursed ~₹20 lakh crore to ~40 crore beneficiaries (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
Stand-Up India Scheme Entrepreneurship/Women 2016 Support women and SC/ST entrepreneurs Provides loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for greenfield enterprises. Mandates at least one woman/SC/ST borrower per bank branch. Eligible: Women, SC/ST entrepreneurs. Supported ~1.8 lakh enterprises (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Scheme for First-Time Women, SC, and ST Entrepreneurs Entrepreneurship/Women 2025 Empower first-time women/SC/ST entrepreneurs Provides loans up to ₹2 crore for startups. Includes training and mentorship. Targets 5 lakh entrepreneurs in first phase. Eligible: Women, SC/ST first-time entrepreneurs. Impacts ~₹10,000 crore startup ecosystem (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
Mahila Coir Yojana MSME/Women 1994 Promote women’s participation in coir industry Provides training, equipment, and working capital for women in coir production (Kerala-focused). Offers 75% subsidy on machinery. Eligible: Women entrepreneurs. Supports ~50,000 women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Udyogini Scheme MSME/Women 1997 Empower women entrepreneurs in rural/urban areas Provides loans up to ₹3 lakh with subsidies for women in manufacturing, services, and trade. Focuses on SC/ST and BPL women. Eligible: Women entrepreneurs (BPL). Supported ~2 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) Skill Development 2015 Train youth for industry-relevant skills Offers short-term training, certification, and placement support. Prioritizes women through special batches and SHG integration. Eligible: Youth, women. Trained ~1.2 crore, ~₹10,000 crore allocated (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) Skill Development 2014 Train rural youth for employment Focuses on market-linked skills for rural poor, with 33% reservation for women. Provides placement support and post-training tracking. Eligible: Rural youth (15–35). Trained ~15 lakh, ~₹5,000 crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) Poverty Alleviation 1995 Provide pensions to elderly, widows, disabled Includes IGNOAPS (elderly), IGNWPS (widows), and IGNDPS (disabled). Offers ₹200–500/month, with women prioritized in widow pension schemes. Eligible: BPL elderly, widows, disabled. Benefits ~3 crore, ~₹10,000 crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) Poverty Alleviation/Women 2011 Promote SHGs, enhance rural livelihoods Forms women-led SHGs, provides microfinance, and promotes livelihoods in agriculture, handicrafts. Includes MKSP for women farmers. Eligible: Rural women. Covers ~10 crore women in SHGs, ~₹20,000 crore credit (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) Education/Women 2015 Prevent female infanticide, promote girls’ education Conducts awareness campaigns, provides financial incentives for girls’ education, and monitors child sex ratio. Focuses on low-CSR districts. Eligible: Girls, families in 405 districts. Improved CSR in ~400 districts (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) Education/Women 2015 Encourage savings for girl child’s future Offers savings scheme with 8% interest, deposits ₹250–1.5 lakh/year. Matures after 21 years or at marriage (post-18). Supports education/marriage. Eligible: Girls under 10. Opened ~1.67 crore accounts (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBV) Education/Women 2004 Provide residential schooling for marginalized girls Offers free education and lodging for SC/ST/OBC girls in educationally backward blocks. Focuses on upper primary/secondary education. Eligible: Girls (SC/ST/OBC). Enrolled ~15 lakh girls (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Education).
Samagra Shiksha Abhiyaan (SSA) Education 2018 Improve school education quality and access Integrates SSA, RMSA, and teacher education. Provides free textbooks, uniforms, and promotes girls’ education via KGBV and scholarships. Eligible: All students (6–18). Covers ~25 crore students, ~₹50,000 crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Education).
Mid-Day Meal Scheme (MDMS) Education/Nutrition 1995 Provide free meals to school children Offers nutritious meals to enhance attendance and nutrition. Covers primary/upper primary students, with women cooks employed. Eligible: School children (6–14). Feeds ~12 crore students (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Education).
Udaan Scheme Education/Women 2014 Enhance girls’ enrollment in engineering institutions Provides free coaching, tablets, and mentorship for girls preparing for JEE. Focuses on bridging school-engineering gaps. Eligible: Girl students (Class 11–12). Supported ~1 lakh girls (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Atal Tinkering Labs Expansion Education/Innovation 2025 Foster innovation and scientific temper in schools Plans 50,000 labs in government schools by 2030. Provides hands-on STEM learning, encourages girls’ participation. Eligible: School students. Impacts ~5 crore students (projected 2030). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Science & Technology).
One Stop Centre (OSC) Scheme Women/Safety 2015 Provide integrated support for women facing violence Offers medical, legal, and psychological aid under one roof. Funded by Nirbhaya Fund, operates 700+ centers across India. Eligible: Women victims of violence. Supported ~10 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Women Helpline Scheme (181) Women/Safety 2015 Provide 24x7 support for women in distress Offers counseling, emergency response, and referrals to OSCs. Linked to police and legal services. Eligible: All women. Handled ~5 lakh calls annually (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Ujjwala Scheme (Trafficking) Women/Safety 2007 Combat trafficking, rehabilitate survivors Provides shelter homes, vocational training, and reintegration support for trafficked women. Focuses on prevention and awareness. Eligible: Trafficking victims. Rescued ~1 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Mahila Shakti Kendra (MSK) Women/Empowerment 2017 Empower rural women through community engagement Promotes skill training, financial inclusion, and leadership. Operates at block level, supports SHGs and local governance. Eligible: Rural women. Impacts ~1 crore women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Subhadra Yojana Women/Welfare 2024 Provide financial assistance to women Offers ₹50,000 over 5 years (₹5,000 biannually) to women aged 21–60 in Odisha. Paid on Raksha Bandhan and Women’s Day. Eligible: EWS women in Odisha. Benefits ~25 lakh women (2025). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Namo Drone Didi Scheme Women/Agriculture 2023 Train women in drone technology for agriculture Provides drone training and equipment to 15,000 women SHGs. ₹1,261 crore allocated for modern farming techniques. Eligible: Women SHGs. Trained ~10,000 women (2025). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Lakhpati Didi Scheme Women/Empowerment 2023 Ensure sustainable income for women SHG members Targets ₹1 lakh annual income for 3 crore women via SHGs. Provides microfinance, skill training, and market linkages. Eligible: SHG women. Covers ~9 crore women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Svamitva Yojana Rural Development/Women 2020 Authenticate rural land records, empower women Uses drones to map rural properties, issues property cards. Promotes women’s property ownership to reduce disputes. Eligible: Rural landowners. Issued ~65 lakh cards (2025). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Land Reforms).
Working Women Hostel Scheme Women/Welfare 1972 Provide safe accommodation for working women Offers subsidized hostels with security, daycare, and basic amenities. Supports women migrating for jobs/education. Eligible: Working women, students. Supports ~1 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Swadhar Greh Scheme Women/Welfare 2002 Provide shelter/support for women in distress Offers shelter, counseling, and vocational training for widows, destitute, and abused women. Operates 400+ homes. Eligible: Women in distress. Supports ~50,000 women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Mahila E-Haat Women/Entrepreneurship 2016 Promote women entrepreneurs via online platform Provides digital marketplace for women to sell products/services. Supports SHGs, NGOs, and individual entrepreneurs. Eligible: Women entrepreneurs. Empowers ~1 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Support to Training and Employment Programme (STEP) Women/Skill Development 1986 Enhance women’s employability through training Provides training in agriculture, IT, handicrafts for marginalized women. Offers stipends and placement support. Eligible: Women (SC/ST/BPL). Trained ~2 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Rajiv Gandhi Scheme for Empowerment of Adolescent Girls (SABLA) Women/Nutrition 2011 Empower adolescent girls through nutrition and skills Provides nutrition (Take Home Ration), health check-ups, and life skills training at Anganwadis. Focuses on 11–18-year-olds. Eligible: Adolescent girls (11–18). Covers ~1 crore girls (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Indira Gandhi Matritva Sahyog Yojana (IGMSY) Women/Health 2010 Compensate wage loss, promote safe delivery Provides ₹4,000 in three installments for pregnant women (19+ years) for first two live births. Merged with PMMVY in some states. Eligible: Pregnant women (19+). Benefits ~1 crore women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Nai Roshni Scheme Women/Minorities 2012 Develop leadership among minority women Offers training in financial literacy, health, legal rights, and digital skills. Run by NGOs and government institutions. Eligible: Minority women. Trained ~5 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) Women/Energy 2016 Provide clean cooking fuel to women Offers free LPG connections to BPL women, reducing indoor pollution. Subsidizes refills for 5 years. Eligible: BPL women. Provided ~8 crore connections (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Atal Pension Yojana (APY) Pension 2015 Provide pension to unorganized sector workers Offers guaranteed pension of ₹1,000–5,000/month. Encourages women in informal sectors to enroll. Eligible: Workers (18–40). Covers ~5 crore subscribers (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Social Justice).
Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) Insurance 2015 Provide affordable life insurance Offers ₹2 lakh cover for ₹330/year premium. Encourages women’s enrollment for financial security. Eligible: Adults (18–50). Covers ~15 crore, ~₹10,000 crore claims (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) Insurance 2015 Provide accident insurance cover Offers ₹2 lakh cover for ₹12/year premium. Covers death/disability, prioritizes women in rural areas. Eligible: Adults (18–70). Covers ~30 crore, ~₹5,000 crore claims (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) Sanitation 2014 Promote cleanliness, eliminate open defecation Builds toilets, promotes hygiene awareness. Prioritizes women’s safety and dignity through toilet access. Eligible: All households. Built ~12 crore toilets, ~₹1.5 lakh crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS2 (Health).
Digital India Programme Digital Infrastructure 2015 Promote digital access, e-governance Connects villages with broadband, promotes digital literacy for women via CSCs. Supports e-NAM for farmers. Eligible: All citizens. Connects ~2.5 lakh villages, ~₹3 lakh crore economy (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Technology).
Make in India Industry 2014 Boost manufacturing, job creation Promotes 25 sectors, attracts FDI, and supports women entrepreneurs via MSME schemes like PMEGP. Eligible: Industries, startups. Attracted ~₹20 lakh crore FDI (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Industry).
Start-up India Entrepreneurship 2016 Promote startups, innovation Offers tax benefits, funding, and mentorship. Supports women-led startups with ₹10,000 crore fund. Eligible: Startups. Supported ~1 lakh startups (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Economy).
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) Rural Infrastructure 2000 Provide all-weather rural roads Connects unconnected villages, supports women’s mobility for work/education. Uses green technologies for sustainability. Eligible: Rural areas. Built ~8 lakh km roads, ~₹2 lakh crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Infrastructure).
National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) Environment 2014 Clean Ganga, improve water quality Funds sewage treatment, river cleaning, and afforestation. Engages women SHGs in awareness and livelihoods. Eligible: Ganga basin areas. Invested ~₹20,000 crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Environment).
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) Agriculture 2007 Promote holistic agricultural development Provides funds to states for agriculture, allied sectors. Supports women farmers through 30% fund allocation. Eligible: Farmers, states. Allocated ~₹50,000 crore (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) Agriculture 2015 Promote organic farming Provides ₹50,000/ha for 3 years to farmers for organic inputs. Supports women farmers via SHGs. Eligible: Farmers. Covers ~10 lakh ha (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) Agriculture 2016 Create unified agricultural market Connects 1,000+ mandis online, ensures transparent pricing. Supports women farmers through FPOs and digital literacy. Eligible: Farmers, traders. Facilitates ~₹2 lakh crore trade (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Mandhan Yojana Agriculture/Pension 2019 Provide pension to small/marginal farmers Offers ₹3,000/month pension post-60 years for farmers contributing ₹55–200/month. Includes women farmers. Eligible: Farmers (18–40). Covers ~2 crore farmers (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Agriculture).
New Swarnima Scheme Women/Entrepreneurship 2002 Provide loans to women from backward classes Offers loans up to ₹2 lakh at 5% interest via NBCFDC. Supports SHGs and individual women entrepreneurs. Eligible: Backward class women. Supported ~1 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Mahila Samridhi Yojana Women/Entrepreneurship 1993 Promote microfinance for backward class women Provides loans via SHGs for small businesses. Implemented by NBCFDC, focuses on SC/ST women. Eligible: SC/ST/BPL women. Supported ~2 lakh women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Women Scientist Scheme (WOS) Women/Science 2002 Encourage women in science and technology Provides research grants and fellowships to women scientists for R&D projects. Eligible: Women scientists. Supported ~5,000 women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Science & Technology).
Women in Science and Engineering (WISE) Women/Science 2010 Increase women’s participation in STEM Offers funding, training, and mentorship for women in scientific research. Run by DST. Eligible: Women scientists/engineers. Supported ~2,000 women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS3 (Science & Technology).
Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAG) Women/Nutrition 2010 Improve nutrition, education for adolescent girls Provides supplementary nutrition, life skills, and health check-ups for out-of-school girls (11–14 years). Eligible: Girls (11–14). Covers ~1 crore girls (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
Nari Shakti Puraskar Women/Empowerment 1999 Recognize women achievers Awards women for contributions in education, health, sports, etc. Encourages leadership and role models. Eligible: Women achievers. Awarded ~500 women (2023). UPSC relevance: GS1 (Social Empowerment).
- Important plans like Five Year Plans and other similar important plans -
Plan Period Objective Key Features Achievements and Impact UPSC Relevance
First Five-Year Plan 1951–1956 Rebuild post-independence economy, focus on agriculture and irrigation Based on Harrod-Domar model. Budget: ₹2,378 crore. Allocations: Irrigation/energy (27.2%), agriculture (17.4%), transport (24%). Emphasized dams (Bhakra, Hirakud) and community development programs. Achieved 3.6% GDP growth (target: 2.1%). Built 5 IITs, UGC. Increased food production by 20%. Per capita income rose 8%. Impact: ~₹2,000 crore invested in irrigation. GS3 (Economy): Early economic planning, agricultural focus.
Second Five-Year Plan 1956–1961 Promote rapid industrialization, strengthen public sector Based on Mahalanobis model. Budget: ₹4,800 crore. Focused on heavy industries (steel, coal), import substitution. Established steel plants at Bhilai (Soviet aid), Durgapur (UK aid), Rourkela (German aid). Achieved 4.1% GDP growth (target: 4.5%). Industrial production up by 25%. Established 3 steel plants. Impact: ~₹3,000 crore industrial investment. Challenges: Balance of payments crisis. GS3 (Economy): Industrialization, public sector role.
Third Five-Year Plan 1961–1966 Achieve self-reliance in agriculture, industry; defense strengthening Budget: ₹7,500 crore. Prioritized agriculture (20% funds), defense post-1962 war. Established IARI, expanded dams (Nagarjuna Sagar). Focused on food self-sufficiency. Achieved 2.6% GDP growth (target: 5.6%). Green Revolution initiated. Food production up by 10%. Impact: ~₹1,500 crore irrigation projects. Challenges: Wars (1962, 1965), droughts. GS3 (Economy, Agriculture): Green Revolution, defense spending.
Plan Holiday 1966–1969 Stabilize economy post-war and drought crises Three annual plans instead of a five-year plan. Budget: ~₹2,200 crore/year. Focused on agriculture, food imports, and price stabilization. Introduced HYV seeds. Increased food grain production by 15% (1966–69). Stabilized prices. Impact: ~₹1,000 crore agricultural investment. Laid foundation for Green Revolution. GS3 (Economy): Economic stabilization, agricultural reforms.
Fourth Five-Year Plan 1969–1974 Achieve growth with stability, reduce poverty Budget: ₹15,902 crore. Focused on Green Revolution, poverty alleviation, and self-reliance. Allocated 18% to agriculture, 22% to industry. Nationalized 14 banks. Achieved 3.3% GDP growth (target: 5.7%). Food production up by 20%. Bank nationalization expanded credit (~₹5,000 crore). Impact: ~₹3,000 crore agricultural growth. Challenges: 1971 war, oil crisis. GS3 (Economy): Bank nationalization, poverty focus.
Fifth Five-Year Plan 1974–1979 Eradicate poverty, achieve self-reliance Budget: ₹39,426 crore. Garibi Hatao slogan. Focused on agriculture, industry, and social justice. Introduced Minimum Needs Programme and DPAP. Terminated early in 1978. Achieved 4.8% GDP growth (target: 4.4%). Reduced poverty by 10%. Food production reached 132 MT. Impact: ~₹10,000 crore social programs. Challenges: Political instability. GS2 (Social Justice), GS3 (Economy): Poverty alleviation.
Rolling Plan 1978–1980 Provide continuity during political transition Interim plan by Janata Government. Budget: ~₹12,000 crore/year. Focused on employment, rural development, and agriculture. Emphasized small-scale industries. Increased rural employment by 5%. Food production up by 10%. Impact: ~₹5,000 crore rural investment. Stabilized economy during transition. GS3 (Economy): Interim planning, rural focus.
Sixth Five-Year Plan 1980–1985 Promote economic growth, modernize industries Budget: ₹97,500 crore. Focused on infrastructure (roads, ports), poverty alleviation, and IRDP. Allocated 25% to energy, 20% to agriculture. Promoted women’s SHGs. Achieved 5.4% GDP growth (target: 5.2%). Reduced poverty by 15%. Infrastructure investment ~₹20,000 crore. Impact: ~₹10,000 crore rural programs. GS3 (Economy): Infrastructure, poverty reduction.
Seventh Five-Year Plan 1985–1990 Enhance productivity, employment, and food security Budget: ₹1,80,000 crore. Focused on agriculture, employment, and technology. Introduced Jawahar Rozgar Yojana. Allocated 22% to industry, 20% to social services. Achieved 6% GDP growth (target: 5%). Food production reached 171 MT. Created ~10 crore jobs. Impact: ~₹15,000 crore employment programs. GS3 (Economy): Employment generation, agricultural growth.
Annual Plans 1990–1992 Manage economic crisis, stabilize economy Budget: ~₹60,000 crore/year. Focused on fiscal discipline, export promotion, and crisis management post-1991 reforms. Prioritized agriculture, small industries. Stabilized economy post-BoP crisis. Exports grew by 20%. Impact: ~₹5,000 crore export promotion. Laid groundwork for liberalization. GS3 (Economy): Economic reforms, liberalization.
Eighth Five-Year Plan 1992–1997 Promote human development, economic reforms Budget: ₹4,34,100 crore. Aligned with 1991 liberalization. Focused on privatization, human development (education, health), and infrastructure. Allocated 26% to social services. Achieved 6.8% GDP growth (target: 5.6%). Literacy rate rose to 65%. Infrastructure investment ~₹1 lakh crore. Impact: ~₹50,000 crore social programs. GS3 (Economy): Liberalization, human development.
Ninth Five-Year Plan 1997–2002 Achieve growth with social justice, equity Budget: ₹8,59,200 crore. Focused on agriculture, poverty alleviation, and employment. Introduced PMGSY, SSA. Allocated 25% to social sectors, 20% to infrastructure. Achieved 5.4% GDP growth (target: 6.5%). Reduced poverty to 26%. Built ~2 lakh km rural roads. Impact: ~₹1.5 lakh crore social investment. GS2 (Social Justice), GS3 (Economy): Poverty, infrastructure.
Tenth Five-Year Plan 2002–2007 Achieve inclusive growth, double per capita income Budget: ₹14,83,000 crore. Focused on education (SSA), health (NRHM), and infrastructure. Targeted 8% GDP growth. Promoted PPP models and women’s SHGs. Achieved 7.7% GDP growth (target: 8%). Literacy rate rose to 74%. Reduced poverty to 21%. Impact: ~₹2 lakh crore infrastructure. Challenges: Regional disparities. GS2 (Social Justice), GS3 (Economy): Inclusive growth.
Eleventh Five-Year Plan 2007–2012 Promote inclusive and faster growth Budget: ₹36,44,718 crore. Theme: “Inclusive Growth.” Focused on education, health, agriculture, and infrastructure. Introduced MGNREGA, NRLM. Allocated 30% to social sectors. Achieved 8% GDP growth (target: 9%). MGNREGA employed ~10 crore households. Literacy rate 74%. Impact: ~₹3 lakh crore social programs. Challenges: 2008 financial crisis. GS2 (Social Justice), GS3 (Economy): MGNREGA, inclusivity.
Twelfth Five-Year Plan 2012–2017 Achieve faster, sustainable, inclusive growth Budget: ₹80,50,123 crore. Theme: “Faster, Sustainable, and More Inclusive Growth.” Focused on infrastructure, health (NHM), education, and sustainability. Promoted Aadhaar, DBT. Achieved 6.7% GDP growth (target: 8%). Reduced poverty to 12%. Built ~₹5 lakh crore infrastructure. Impact: ~₹2 lakh crore social schemes. Last FYP before NITI Aayog. GS2 (Governance), GS3 (Economy): Sustainability, DBT.
Three-Year Action Agenda 2017–2020 Provide short-term policy framework post-FYP Introduced by NITI Aayog to replace FYPs. Focused on economic growth, social inclusion, and governance. Prioritized agriculture (doubling farmers’ income), health, and digitalization. Supported schemes like PM-KISAN, Ayushman Bharat. Achieved ~₹1 lakh crore agricultural credit. Impact: ~₹50,000 crore social programs. Set stage for Vision 2020–23. GS3 (Economy): NITI Aayog, short-term planning.
Strategy for New India @75 2018–2022 Outline roadmap for India’s development by 2022 NITI Aayog’s vision document. Focused on 41 sectors: agriculture, health, education, infrastructure, and inclusion. Targeted doubling farmers’ income, 100% literacy, and 9% GDP growth. Increased agricultural credit to ~₹15 lakh crore. Improved health coverage via Ayushman Bharat (~50 crore beneficiaries). Impact: ~₹2 lakh crore infrastructure projects. GS3 (Economy): Long-term vision, inclusivity.
India Vision 2020 2002–2020 Transform India into a developed nation by 2020 Proposed by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and Planning Commission. Focused on technology, education, health, and infrastructure. Targeted 100% literacy, poverty below 5%, and 10% GDP growth. Achieved 74% literacy, reduced poverty to ~12%. Built ~₹10 lakh crore infrastructure. Impact: ~₹5 lakh crore social sector investment. Challenges: Missed poverty, growth targets. GS3 (Economy): Vision planning, development goals.
India Vision 2035 2020–2035 Position India as a $10 trillion economy by 2035 NITI Aayog’s long-term vision. Focuses on sustainable growth, health, education, and technology. Targets zero poverty, 100% renewable energy integration, and women’s empowerment. Supports schemes like PM-KUSUM, NEP. Invested ~₹2 lakh crore in renewables (2023). Impact: ~₹1 lakh crore education/health programs. Ongoing implementation. GS3 (Economy): Sustainable development, long-term goals.
National Manufacturing Policy 2011–Ongoing Enhance manufacturing, create jobs Aims to increase manufacturing’s GDP share to 25% by 2025. Supports Make in India, promotes industrial corridors, and women-led MSMEs. Budget: ~₹1 lakh crore for industrial parks. Created ~2 crore jobs. Attracted ~₹20 lakh crore FDI (2023). Impact: ~₹50,000 crore PLI schemes. Challenges: Global competition. GS3 (Economy): Industrial growth, Make in India.
National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) 2019–2025 Boost infrastructure development ₹111 lakh crore plan covering energy, roads, railways, and urban infrastructure. Promotes PPP models, women’s employment in construction. Includes Gati Shakti for coordination. Completed ~₹20 lakh crore projects (2023). Built ~50,000 km highways. Impact: ~₹10 lakh crore urban infra. Supports ~5 crore jobs. GS3 (Economy): Infrastructure, Gati Shakti.
Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan 2020–Ongoing Promote self-reliance, economic recovery post-COVID ₹20 lakh crore package for MSMEs, agriculture, health, and infrastructure. Includes PLI schemes, PM-KISAN, and women-centric programs like Lakhpati Didi. Disbursed ~₹10 lakh crore to MSMEs. Supported ~12 crore farmers via PM-KISAN. Impact: ~₹5 lakh crore economic stimulus (2023). GS3 (Economy): Self-reliance, economic recovery.
